'''''Mathematical Methods of Classical Mechanics''''' (title of the original in Russian: '''''Математические методы классической механики''''') is a 1974 textbook by mathematician [[Vladimir I. Arnold]]. Originally written in Russian, an English translation was produced in 1978 by [[A. Weinstein]] and [[Vogtmann|K. Vogtmann]].<ref>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=J4nk1U3qjh0C |title=Mathematical Lives: Protagonists of the Twentieth Century From Hilbert to Wiles |publisher=Springer Science & Business Media |year=2010 |isbn=9783642136061 |pages=211}}</ref> It is aimed at [[graduate student]]s.

== Contents ==
* Part I: Newtonian Mechanics
** Chapter 1: Experimental Facts
** Chapter 2: Investigation of the Equations of Motion
* Part II: [[Lagrangian mechanics|Lagrangian Mechanics]]
** Chapter 3: [[Calculus of variations|Variational Principles]]
** Chapter 4: Lagrangian Mechanics on Manifolds
** Chapter 5: Oscillations
** Chapter 6: [[Rigid body|Rigid Bodies]]
* Part III: [[Hamiltonian mechanics|Hamiltonian Mechanics]]
** Chapter 7: [[Differential form|Differential forms]]
** Chapter 8: [[Symplectic manifold|Symplectic Manifolds]]
** Chapter 9: Canonical Formalism
** Chapter 10: Introduction to Perturbation Theory
* Appendices
** Riemannian curvature
** Geodesics of left-invariant metrics on Lie groups and the hydrodynamics of ideal fluids
** Symplectic structures on algebraic manifolds
** Contact structures
** Dynamical systems with symmetries
** Normal forms of quadratic Hamiltonians
** Normal forms of Hamiltonian systems near stationary points and closed trajectories
** Theory of perturbations of conditionally period motion and Kolmogorov's theorem
** Poincaré's geometric theorem, its generalizations and applications
** Multiplicities of characteristic frequencies, and ellipsoids depending on parameters
** Short wave asymptotics
** Lagrangian singularities
** The [[Korteweg–de Vries equation|Kortweg-de Vries equation]]
** Poisson structures
** On elliptic coordinates
** Singularities of ray systems

==Russian original and translations==
The original Russian first edition ''Математические методы классической механики'' was published in 1974 by [[Nauka (publisher)|Наука]]. A second edition was published in 1979, and a third in 1989. The book has since been translated into a number of other languages, including French, German, Japanese and Mandarin.

== Reviews ==
The ''[[Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society]]'' said, "The [book] under review [...] written by a distinguished mathematician [...is one of] the first textbooks [to] successfully to present to students of mathematics and physics, [sic] classical mechanics in a modern setting."<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Sneddon|first=Ian N.|author-link=Ian Sneddon|date=March 1980|title=Book Review of Mathematical methods of classical mechanics and A course in mathematical physics, vol. 1: Classical dynamical systems|url=https://projecteuclid.org/download/pdf_1/euclid.bams/1183546243|journal=[[Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society]]|volume=2|issue=2|pages=346–352|doi=10.1090/S0273-0979-1980-14755-2|via=[[Project Euclid]]|doi-access=free}}</ref>

A book review in the journal ''Celestial Mechanics'' said, "In summary, the author has succeeded in producing a mathematical synthesis of the science of dynamics. The book is well presented and beautifully translated [...] Arnold's book is pure poetry; one does not simply read it, one enjoys it."<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Broucke|first=R|author-link= Roger A. Broucke |date=1982|title=Book-Review - Mathematical Methods of Classical Mechanics|url=http://adsabs.harvard.edu/full/1982CeMec..28..345A|journal=Celestial Mechanics|volume=28|pages=345|via=[[SAO/NASA ADS]]|doi=10.1007/bf01243742|bibcode=1982CeMec..28..345A|s2cid=189830621}}</ref>
